syllabus_topics: Real numbers: algebraic, order, and supremum axioms.
Sequences: the concept of limit; applications.
Real functions of a real variable; limits and continuity; elementary functions.
Global properties of continuous functions: intermediate value and Weierstrass theorems.
Integration: by parts, by substitution, rational functions.
Applications: calculation of areas; definition of functions (e.g., logarithm, error, and gamma functions); examples of separable differential equations of the form f(y) y’(t) = g(t).
Taylor series: definition, examples, and convergence.
assessment_rules: The final grade in the normal period is calculated as 30% from the first MAP45, 30% from the second MAP45, and 40% from the final exam. The final grade in the recourse period will be the maximum of this formula or the recourse exam (100%). Alternatively, one MAP45 or the first exam can be recovered in the recourse period, with the best score counting. Grades equal to or above 17.5 will be subject to oral confirmation. An optional assessment component from study sessions can add 1 point to the final grade if the exam grade is between 9 and 14.
